topics.title: Introduction and Key Definitions
explain: AS 14 (Revised) governs accounting for amalgamations in the books of the transferee company.
Amalgamation includes mergers under the Companies Act, 2013 or other applicable statutes.
Transferor company is the company that gets amalgamated into another entity.
Transferee company is the company into which the transferor company is amalgamated.
Acquisitions where the acquired company maintains its separate existence are outside AS 14.
topics.example: When X Ltd merges into Y Ltd and X Ltd dissolves, X Ltd is the transferor and Y Ltd is the transferee.
remember: AS 14 applies only to the books of the transferee company.
Acquisitions without company dissolution are not covered by AS 14.
mistakes: Applying AS 14 rules to acquisitions where the acquired entity continues to exist.

quiz.q: Which entity's financial accounting is specifically governed by AS 14 (Revised)?
o: Both Transferor and Transferee companies equally
quiz.why: AS 14 deals specifically with the accounting to be made in the books of the transferee company.

quiz.q: Why are simple corporate acquisitions excluded from AS 14?
o: Because the acquired entity is not dissolved
Because consideration is not paid in cash
quiz.why: Acquisitions leave the acquired entity intact, whereas AS 14 covers amalgamations involving entity dissolution.

topics.title: Amalgamation in the Nature of Merger
explain: An amalgamation is a merger only if it satisfies five strict conditions simultaneously.
Condition 1: All assets and liabilities of the transferor become those of the transferee.
Condition 2: Shareholders holding at least 90% equity face value become equity holders of transferee.
Condition 3: Consideration to equity holders is paid strictly in equity shares, except cash for fractions.
Condition 4: The transferor company's business is intended to be carried on by the transferee.
Condition 5: No book value adjustments are made except to align accounting policies.

flow.title: Testing for Merger Qualification
steps: Check consideration paid in equity shares

topics.example: A Ltd merges into B Ltd; 95% of A Ltd shareholders take B Ltd equity shares and business continues at existing book values.
remember: All 5 conditions must be fulfilled simultaneously to qualify as a merger.
Cash can only be paid for fractional shares under merger consideration.
mistakes: Treating an amalgamation as a merger when only 4 out of 5 conditions are fulfilled.

quiz.q: What minimum percentage of transferor equity face value must become equity holders in transferee for a merger?
quiz.why: AS 14 mandates that shareholders holding not less than 90% of equity face value must become equity shareholders of the transferee.

quiz.q: When can cash be legally paid to equity shareholders in a merger amalgamation?
quiz.why: Under merger conditions, consideration must be in equity shares except cash paid for fractional shares.

topics.title: Amalgamation in Nature of Purchase and Accounting Methods
explain: An amalgamation is in the nature of purchase if it fails any one of the 5 merger conditions.
In purchase nature, one company acquires another company as a business acquisition.
Pooling of Interests Method is used exclusively for amalgamations in the nature of merger.
Under pooling of interests, assets, liabilities, and reserves are recorded at existing book values.
Purchase Method is used for amalgamations in the nature of purchase.
Under purchase method, assets and liabilities are recorded at book values or agreed fair values.

flow.title: Selecting Accounting Method
steps: If Yes use Pooling of Interests

topics.example: P Ltd takes over Q Ltd and revalues land to fair value; it fails merger condition 5, so Purchase Method is used.
remember: Merger nature uses Pooling of Interests Method.
mistakes: Using Pooling of Interests Method when assets are taken over at revised fair values.

quiz.q: Which accounting method must be used if an amalgamation fails one merger condition?
quiz.why: Failing any merger condition classifies the transaction as a purchase, requiring the Purchase Method.

quiz.q: How are assets and liabilities recorded under the Pooling of Interests Method?
quiz.why: Pooling of interests records assets, liabilities, and reserves at their existing carrying amounts.

topics.title: Purchase Consideration
explain: Purchase consideration is the aggregate of shares, securities, and cash paid to shareholders.
Consideration is paid strictly to the shareholders (equity and preference) of the transferor.
Payments made to debenture holders or creditors are excluded from purchase consideration.
Net Payment Method calculates consideration by summing all payments to equity and preference holders.
Net Assets Method calculates consideration as Net Assets taken over when Net Payment cannot be used.
Net Payment Method must be preferred whenever payment details are explicitly available.

flow.title: Calculating Purchase Consideration
steps: Sum up to get Purchase Consideration

topics.example: Company A issues ₹4,20,000 equity shares and ₹1,87,000 preference shares to B Ltd shareholders; PC is ₹6,07,000.
remember: Purchase consideration includes payments to shareholders only.
Debenture discharge payments are not part of purchase consideration.
mistakes: Including debenture conversion amounts into the purchase consideration calculation.

quiz.q: Payments made to which group are included in Purchase Consideration under AS 14?
quiz.why: AS 14 defines consideration as payments made specifically to the shareholders of the transferor company.

quiz.q: How is purchase consideration calculated if payment amounts to shareholders are given?
quiz.why: Net Payment Method must be used first to compute PC whenever payments to shareholders are given.

topics.title: Treatment of Reserves and Statutory Reserves
explain: In a merger, the identity of all reserves of the transferor company is fully preserved.
In a purchase, general reserves of the transferor lose their identity and are not recorded.
Statutory reserves must retain their identity even under the purchase method if required by law.
Statutory reserves are recorded by debiting 'Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve' in transferee books.
Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve is shown as a negative balance under Reserves and Surplus.
When the statutory requirement expires, both the statutory reserve and adjustment account are reversed.

flow.title: Accounting for Statutory Reserves in Purchase Method
steps: Credit Statutory Reserve in transferee books
Reverse both accounts when law permits

topics.example: Transferee company takes over ₹100 lakhs Investment Allowance Reserve by debiting Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve for ₹100 lakhs.
remember: Statutory reserves must be maintained in purchase method if required by statutes.
Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve is presented as a negative reserve.
mistakes: Setting off Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve against General Reserve or Statutory Reserve.

quiz.q: How is Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve presented in the transferee company's Balance Sheet?
o: As a negative balance under Reserves and Surplus
quiz.why: It is a reserve account carrying a debit balance, presented as a negative line item under Reserves and Surplus.

quiz.q: What happens to the statutory reserve identity in an amalgamation in the nature of merger?
o: It is credited to P&L account
quiz.why: In a merger, the identity of all reserves (including statutory reserves) is preserved.

topics.title: Treatment of Goodwill, Capital Reserve, and P&L Balance
explain: In purchase method, if Consideration > Net Assets acquired, the difference is debited to Goodwill.
If Net Assets acquired > Consideration, the difference is credited to Capital Reserve.
Goodwill arising on amalgamation should be amortised to income over its useful life.
Useful life of goodwill should not exceed 5 years unless a longer period is justified.
In a merger, transferor's P&L balance is combined with transferee's P&L or transferred to General Reserve.
In a purchase, transferor's P&L balance loses its identity completely and is not recorded.
topics.example: Consideration paid is ₹1,650 lakhs for Net Assets of ₹1,540 lakhs; the excess ₹110 lakhs is Goodwill.
remember: Standard amortisation period for Goodwill on amalgamation is max 5 years.
Transferor's P&L balance loses identity in purchase method.
mistakes: Carrying forward the transferor's P&L credit balance into transferee's books under purchase method.

quiz.q: What is the normal maximum period for amortising goodwill arising on amalgamation under AS 14?
quiz.why: AS 14 specifies that goodwill arising on amalgamation should be amortised over a period not exceeding 5 years unless justified.

quiz.q: In purchase accounting, what does excess of Net Assets over Purchase Consideration represent?
quiz.why: When net assets acquired exceed purchase consideration, the positive difference is credited to Capital Reserve.

topics.title: Disclosures and Post Balance Sheet Amalgamation
explain: All amalgamations require disclosure of company names, business nature, effective date, and method used.
Merger disclosures require details of shares issued and percentage of equity exchanged.
Purchase disclosures require consideration details and goodwill amortisation period.
Amalgamations effected after balance sheet date but before financial statement approval are disclosed per AS 4.
Post balance sheet amalgamations are not incorporated into current financial statement figures.
Adjustment to financial statements occurs only if amalgamation impacts going concern assumption.

flow.title: Handling Post Balance Sheet Amalgamation
steps: Do not adjust B/S financial figures
Disclose event in notes per AS 4
Adjust figures only if going concern fails

topics.example: An amalgamation occurs on April 10 before March 31 accounts are approved; it is disclosed in notes per AS 4 without altering March 31 figures.
remember: Post balance sheet amalgamations are non-adjusting events under AS 4.
Disclosure in notes to accounts is mandatory for post B/S date amalgamations.
mistakes: Incorporating post balance sheet amalgamation figures into current year's financial statements.

quiz.q: How should an amalgamation occurring after the balance sheet date but before statement approval be treated?
o: Disclosed in notes per AS 4 without adjusting figures
quiz.why: It is a post-balance sheet event covered by AS 4, requiring disclosure in notes rather than figure adjustments.

quiz.q: Which additional disclosure is required specifically for Pooling of Interests Method?
quiz.why: Mergers require disclosing the percentage of equity shares exchanged to effect the amalgamation.
